blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A plugin's ExportStep extends the host's Step class and declares `@Override protected void beforeWrite(Batch b)`. It was compiled against host API 2.0. Host 3.0 changes the method in Step to `beforeWrite(Batch b, Context c)`, and the plugin jar, not recompiled, is dropped into a 3.0 host. What happens when the host runs the step?

options.text: The host refuses to load ExportStep, since the JVM repeats the @Override check when it loads the class
options.says: the check happens only when javac compiles the subclass; the annotated Backoff compiled against version 1 ran against version 2 without complaint

options.text: The host loads ExportStep and runs Step's own beforeWrite, since the plugin's method is now one that nothing calls
options.says: against the new supertype the old method is a new method of the subclass; the swapped-jar run printed the base class's delays

options.text: The host loads ExportStep and runs the plugin's beforeWrite, since the JVM picks an override by its name
options.says: a method overrides by its signature, name and parameter types; the base class's version ran

options.text: The host refuses to load ExportStep, since the compiled class records which method it overrides
options.says: the annotation is checked by javac and has SOURCE retention; the class loaded and ran with the base method

origin.section: @Override Turns a Method That Stopped Overriding into a Compile Error

questions.stem: A team compiles with `javac -Werror` and no -Xlint option. Their code calls `Cache.evictAll()`, which library 2.3 annotates `@Deprecated(since = "2.3")`. Library 2.6 changes it to `@Deprecated(since = "2.3", forRemoval = true)`. How does their build end against 2.3, and against 2.6?

options.text: It passes against 2.3 and fails against 2.6, since only the second version's call is reported as a warning
options.says: a plain deprecated use is folded into a note, which -Werror doesn't count; a forRemoval use is a [removal] warning by default

options.text: It fails against 2.3 and against 2.6, since -Werror turns each deprecation report into an error
options.says: the plain deprecation shows up as a note, not a warning, and -Werror ignored it in the Checkout run

options.text: It passes against 2.3 and against 2.6, since forRemoval only changes what the documentation says
options.says: forRemoval changes javac's report from a note to a [removal] warning at every use

options.text: It passes against 2.3 and against 2.6, since javac reports a removal only when -Xlint:removal is given
options.says: the [removal] warning appeared with a plain javac, with no -Xlint option

origin.section: A Use of a forRemoval Element Warns by Default; Plain Deprecation Is Only a Note

questions.stem: A method carries `@SuppressWarnings("deprecation")`. It calls `client.connect()`, annotated plain `@Deprecated`, and `client.legacyAuth()`, annotated `@Deprecated(forRemoval = true)`. The build runs `javac -Xlint:deprecation`. What does javac report for this method?

options.text: No warning, since the suppression key covers both kinds of deprecated call
options.says: removal is its own key; the method with the "deprecation" suppression in Refunds still got the [removal] warning

options.text: One warning, for legacyAuth, since the suppression key covers only the other kind of call
options.says: "deprecation" silences plain deprecation; a forRemoval use needs "removal"

options.text: One warning, for connect, since the -Xlint option overrides the suppression for that kind of call
options.says: the annotation silenced charge under -Xlint:deprecation; what was reported was the removal

options.text: Two warnings, since the -Xlint option overrides the suppression for both kinds of call
options.says: the annotation silenced the plain deprecation even with -Xlint:deprecation

origin.section: A Use of a forRemoval Element Warns by Default; Plain Deprecation Is Only a Note

questions.stem: A class carries `@SuppressWarnings("all")`, and the IDE shows no warnings for it. One of its methods casts an `Object` to `Map<String, Long>`. The CI build runs `javac -Xlint:all -Werror`. What does the build do?

options.text: It fails on the cast, since javac treats the key as one it doesn't know and suppresses nothing
options.says: javac 21 ignores unknown keys without a word, and "all" is not one of its keys; the [unchecked] warning stayed

options.text: It fails with an error about the key, since javac rejects a key it doesn't know
options.says: javac said nothing about "uncheked" or "all"; it only reported the cast

options.text: It passes, since the key suppresses every lint category in javac as it does in the IDE
options.says: "all" is not a javac 21 key; javac still reported the unchecked cast

options.text: It passes, since a class-level suppression reaches every member under any key
options.says: the scope reaches every member, but a key javac doesn't know suppresses nothing anywhere

origin.section: @SuppressWarnings Covers Its Whole Declaration, Including Warnings Added Later

questions.stem: `loadRoutes(Object tree)` carries `@SuppressWarnings("unchecked")` for one cast of `tree` to `Map<String, List<String>>`. A later commit adds, in the same method, a raw `List` stored into that map. The build runs `javac -Xlint:unchecked`. What does it report for the new line?

options.text: Nothing, since the annotation applies to every line of the method, the new one included
options.says: a suppression covers everything inside the declaration that carries it, code added later included

options.text: Nothing, since a raw type is reported under rawtypes and never under unchecked
options.says: storing a raw List into a Map<String, List<...>> is an unchecked conversion; the local-variable version reported two [unchecked] warnings

options.text: An unchecked warning, since the annotation applies only to the line it was written for
options.says: the annotation is on the method, so it covers every line of it; the method-level Ports compiled silently

options.text: An unchecked warning, since -Xlint:unchecked reports lines added after the annotation
options.says: javac doesn't know when a line was written; the method-level Ports compiled silently with -Xlint:unchecked

origin.section: @SuppressWarnings Covers Its Whole Declaration, Including Warnings Added Later

concepts: The @Override check runs only when the subclass compiles; a class compiled against one version of its supertype and run against another gets no check, and the supertype's method runs.
@SuppressWarnings("deprecation") doesn't silence a [removal] warning, which needs "removal"; a deprecated caller and an overriding method still get removal warnings.
javac reports each use of a forRemoval element as a [removal] warning by default, while plain deprecated uses are folded into a note that -Werror doesn't count until -Xlint:deprecation lists them.
A suppression covers everything inside the declaration that carries it, including code added later; on a local variable it covers one declaration.
javac ignores @SuppressWarnings keys it doesn't know, "all" included, without a warning.
